<description>
The `tapscript/disabled_checkmultisig` and `tapscript/disabled_checkmultisigverify` spenders in `feature_taproot.py` run `OP_CHECKMULTISIG(VERIFY)` on a Schnorr signature (`0 OP_SWAP 1 <pubkey> 1 OP_CHECKMULTISIG`). An implementation which forgets to disable these opcodes in tapscript still fails the case, because a 64 byte Schnorr signature is not a valid DER signature. So the asset tests generated from these spenders cannot tell whether the opcodes are disabled. This came up while running `script_assets_test.json` against a third-party implementation which executed `OP_CHECKMULTISIG` in tapscript and passed every case.

This PR does two things:

1. Adds a 0-of-0 variant for both opcodes (`OP_DROP 0 0 0 OP_CHECKMULTISIG` and `OP_DROP 0 0 0 OP_CHECKMULTISIGVERIFY 1`). It needs no signature and leaves a single `1` on the stack, so it succeeds when the opcode is executed and fails only because of the tapscript rule. Checked against the implementation above: it accepts the new failure case while its fixed version rejects it with `SCRIPT_ERR_TAPSCRIPT_CHECKMULTISIG`.

2. Writes the expected script error of a failure case into the JSON dump (`"error"`), taken from the `err_msg` the spender already declares and which `block_submit` already checks against the node. `script_assets_test` then checks the error under exactly the listed flags. Until now a failure case could only be checked for failing, not for failing for the stated reason. A superset of the flags may fail earlier for another reason, so the check is limited to the exact flag set. Consumers which do not know the field are unaffected, and spenders without `err_msg` get no field.

Verified by running `feature_taproot.py --dumptests` and `test_bitcoin --run_test=script_assets_tests` on the regenerated dump (2897 vectors, 2410 of them with an `error` field).
</description>

<commits>
420decb170 test: strengthen the tapscript CHECKMULTISIG asset tests and dump the expected error

The tapscript/disabled_checkmultisig(verify) failure cases run
OP_CHECKMULTISIG(VERIFY) on a Schnorr signature. An implementation which
does not disable the opcodes in tapscript still fails them, because a
Schnorr signature is not a valid DER signature, so these cases cannot
tell whether the opcodes are disabled. Add a 0-of-0 variant, which
succeeds when the opcode is executed, so that only the tapscript rule can
make it fail.

Also write the expected script error of a failure case to the JSON dump
when the spender declares one, and check it in script_assets_test under
exactly the listed flags. The failure cases could so far only be checked
for failing, not for failing for the right reason. Consumers which do not
know the new field are unaffected.
</commits>

diff --git a/src/test/script_assets_tests.cpp b/src/test/script_assets_tests.cpp
index 56d52edc75..3d97a83847 100644
--- a/src/test/script_assets_tests.cpp
+++ b/src/test/script_assets_tests.cpp
@@ -5,6 +5,7 @@
 #include <primitives/transaction.h>
 #include <script/interpreter.h>
 #include <script/script.h>
+#include <script/script_error.h>
 #include <script/sigcache.h>
 #include <script/sign.h>
 #include <script/signingprovider.h>
@@ -139,8 +140,14 @@ static void AssetTest(const UniValue& test, SignatureCache& signature_cache)
         for (const auto flags : ALL_CONSENSUS_FLAGS) {
             // If a test is supposed to fail with test_flags, it should also fail with any superset thereof.
             if ((flags & test_flags) == test_flags) {
-                bool ret = VerifyScript(tx.vin[idx].scriptSig, prevouts[idx].scriptPubKey, &tx.vin[idx].scriptWitness, flags, txcheck, nullptr);
+                ScriptError serror;
+                bool ret = VerifyScript(tx.vin[idx].scriptSig, prevouts[idx].scriptPubKey, &tx.vin[idx].scriptWitness, flags, txcheck, &serror);
                 BOOST_CHECK(!ret);
+                // With exactly test_flags the failure is also expected for the stated reason. A superset of the
+                // flags may fail earlier for another reason.
+                if (flags == test_flags && test.exists("error")) {
+                    BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL(ScriptErrorString(serror), test["error"].get_str());
+                }
             }
         }
     }
diff --git a/test/functional/feature_taproot.py b/test/functional/feature_taproot.py
index 188d201142..214451696d 100755
--- a/test/functional/feature_taproot.py
+++ b/test/functional/feature_taproot.py
@@ -1029,6 +1029,10 @@ def spenders_taproot_active():
         ("t35", CScript([bytes([csa_low_val]), pubs[1], OP_CHECKSIGADD, csa_low_result, OP_EQUAL])),
         # 36) Empty script
         ("t36", CScript([])),
+        # 37) 0-of-0 CHECKMULTISIG, which succeeds when executed, so only the tapscript ban can make it fail
+        ("t37", CScript([OP_DROP, OP_0, OP_0, OP_0, OP_CHECKMULTISIG])),
+        # 38) The same with CHECKMULTISIGVERIFY
+        ("t38", CScript([OP_DROP, OP_0, OP_0, OP_0, OP_CHECKMULTISIGVERIFY, OP_1])),
     ]
     # Add many dummies to test huge trees
     for j in range(100000):
@@ -1047,6 +1051,10 @@ def spenders_taproot_active():
     # Test that OP_CHECKMULTISIG and OP_CHECKMULTISIGVERIFY cause failure, but OP_CHECKSIG and OP_CHECKSIGVERIFY work.
     add_spender(spenders, "tapscript/disabled_checkmultisig", leaf="t1", **common, **SINGLE_SIG, failure={"leaf": "t3"}, **ERR_TAPSCRIPT_CHECKMULTISIG)
     add_spender(spenders, "tapscript/disabled_checkmultisigverify", leaf="t2", **common, **SINGLE_SIG, failure={"leaf": "t4"}, **ERR_TAPSCRIPT_CHECKMULTISIG)
+    # The same with a 0-of-0 CHECKMULTISIG(VERIFY), which succeeds if the opcode is executed. An implementation which
+    # does not disable the opcode fails the t3/t4 variants anyway, since the Schnorr signature is not a DER signature.
+    add_spender(spenders, "tapscript/disabled_checkmultisig", leaf="t1", **common, **SINGLE_SIG, failure={"leaf": "t37"}, **ERR_TAPSCRIPT_CHECKMULTISIG)
+    add_spender(spenders, "tapscript/disabled_checkmultisigverify", leaf="t2", **common, **SINGLE_SIG, failure={"leaf": "t38"}, **ERR_TAPSCRIPT_CHECKMULTISIG)
     # Test that OP_IF and OP_NOTIF do not accept non-0x01 as truth value (the MINIMALIF rule is consensus in Tapscript)
     add_spender(spenders, "tapscript/minimalif", leaf="t5", **common, inputs=[getter("sign"), b'\x01'], failure={"inputs": [getter("sign"), b'\x02']}, **ERR_TAPSCRIPT_MINIMALIF)
     add_spender(spenders, "tapscript/minimalnotif", leaf="t6", **common, inputs=[getter("sign"), b'\x01'], failure={"inputs": [getter("sign"), b'\x03']}, **ERR_TAPSCRIPT_MINIMALIF)
@@ -1400,6 +1408,9 @@ def dump_json_test(tx, input_utxos, idx, success, failure):
         fields.append(("success", dump_witness(success)))
     if failure is not None:
         fields.append(("failure", dump_witness(failure)))
+        # The script error the failure case is expected to fail with under the listed flags, when known.
+        if spender.err_msg is not None:
+            fields.append(("error", spender.err_msg))
 
     # Write the dump to $TEST_DUMP_DIR/x/xyz... where x,y,z,... are the SHA1 sum of the dump (which makes the
     # file naming scheme compatible with fuzzing infrastructure).

</patch>
